title: Assessing Ocular Blood Flow During Water Drinking Test Using Laser Speckle Flowgraphy
author: Tong Boon Tang
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.impcc5n

steps.title: Familiarize participants with LSFG system
steps.instruction: Explain the LSFG‑NAVI system (Softcare Co., Ltd., Japan) and all procedural details to each subject before starting the experiment.

steps.title: Adjust LSFG system and allow relaxation
steps.instruction: Adjust the LSFG‑NAVI system to the eye position of the participant, then give the subject sufficient time to relax before any recording.

steps.title: Prepare darkroom for recordings
steps.instruction: Ensure that all LSFG recordings are performed in a darkroom environment.

steps.title: Acquire baseline LSFG recordings
steps.instruction: Before water intake, acquire three consecutive LSFG recordings; compute the average of these three values for later analysis.

steps.title: Administer water drinking test
steps.instruction: Instruct the participant to drink the entire 1 liter (1000 mL) of water within a few minutes.

steps.title: Perform post‑water LSFG recordings
steps.instruction: Record LSFG data at 10‑minute intervals after the start of water intake, continuing until 60 minutes post‑intake (recordings at 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, and 60 minutes). At each time point, acquire three consecutive recordings and use their average for analysis.

substeps.instruction: Start the first post‑water recording 10 minutes after water consumption began.
Repeat recordings every 10 minutes up to 60 minutes.
At each time point, collect three consecutive recordings and calculate their mean.

steps.title: Compute MBR pulse waveforms and heart rate
steps.instruction: Using the proprietary LSFG analysis software, compute mean blur rate (MBR) pulse waveforms for the entire optic nerve head (ONH) and the avascular region; segment the ONH into vascular and tissue areas and compute MBR for each sub‑region. Also compute heart rate from the MBR waveform.

substeps.instruction: Select the whole ONH as a region of interest (ROI) and calculate its MBR.
Select the avascular region as an ROI and calculate its MBR.
Segment the ONH into vascular and tissue components and calculate MBR for each.
Derive heart rate from the MBR pulse waveform.

steps.title: Export and normalize data
steps.instruction: Export the pulse waveform parameters for the whole ONH, vascular ONH, tissue ONH, and avascular region, as well as heart rate, then normalize each participant’s values to their own baseline measurements.

steps.title: Statistical analysis in SPSS
steps.instruction: Import the normalized data into SPSS, visually inspect distributions with histograms, QQ plots, and box plots; because data are non‑normal, perform a two‑tailed Wilcoxon Signed Rank test with significance set at P < 0.05.

substeps.instruction: Create histograms, QQ plots, and box plots to assess normality.
Run Wilcoxon Signed Rank test (asymptotic significance, two‑tailed).
Interpret results using a significance threshold of P < 0.05.
